# A grouped block whose `Transaction` guid is not a guid.
#
# `_refuse_a_payment_guid_nothing_can_parse` reads `txn_guid:` and
# `txn_split_guid:` out of the block's keys, and the directives carry theirs
# somewhere else — so the new spelling had no equivalent of the guard whose
# whole point is that a mistyped guid "says which split settles which record,
# which is not a thing to guess at".
#
# Two ways it bit, and the block states no `memo:` so that neither is masked
# (a stated memo normalises the guid on the way past, by accident):
#
#   - where the record otherwise matched, `_the_book_holds` swallowed the parse
#     error, the block scored one bare slot, the run said `unchanged`, and the
#     mistyped line was read by nobody — the silent unread line this format
#     refuses every other spelling of;
#   - where it did not, the rebuild ran first: `Unpost(False)` destroyed the
#     posting, and only then did the guid fail to parse.
#
# What this fixture produces: a refusal naming the guid, before anything is
# unposted.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
invoice "INV-USD-001"
  customer_id: "C-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-05
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-05
    description: "Consulting"
    action: "Hours"
    account: "Income:Sales"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
    tax_included: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-05
    due: 2026-02-05
    ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
    memo: "Invoice INV-USD-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-02-27
    amount: 100
    account: "Assets:Bank:USD"
    Transaction "not-a-guid"
      PaymentSplit "708192a3b4c5d6e7f809122334455667"
